title: Tornado
description: Use this list before tornado season - warnings give minutes, not hours, so your shelter and alerts must be ready in advance.

items.text: Pick your shelter: a safe room or storm shelter, then a basement, then a small interior windowless room on the lowest floor (closet, bathroom, or hallway)
Know the alerts: a Tornado Watch means be ready to move; a Tornado Warning means go to shelter now - do not wait to see it
Keep a NOAA Weather Radio with battery backup, programmed with your county SAME code
Turn on Wireless Emergency Alerts on every phone and sign up for local alerts - outdoor sirens often cannot be heard indoors
If you live in a mobile home, go to a sturdy building or community shelter on any day a Watch is issued or severe storms are forecast
Practice getting everyone, including pets, to shelter in under 2 minutes
Keep a helmet (bike, sports, or motorcycle) for each person in the shelter - head injuries cause many tornado deaths
Keep sturdy shoes for each person in the shelter for walking over glass and nails afterward
Keep a mattress, heavy blankets, or sleeping bags at hand to cover heads and bodies
In a basement, plan to get under a workbench, heavy table, or the stairs - not under heavy items on the floor above
Keep a flashlight and extra batteries in the shelter
Keep a battery or hand-crank radio in the shelter
Keep phones charged and nearby during storm season, especially at night
Keep a whistle in the shelter to signal rescuers if trapped
Keep a first aid kit and needed medicines in or near the shelter
Keep water and some non-perishable food in the shelter (at least a few days' worth for a safe room)
Know the car rule: never shelter under an overpass or bridge
Keep work gloves and N95 masks for safe cleanup through debris
Set a family meeting point in case you are separated after the storm
Pick an out-of-area contact - local lines overload after a tornado, so text instead of calling
